answer: Reputation Canopy Splitting. Each identity’s visible reputation is capped by a vertex count of independent, paid interaction histories; cloning splits that canopy, so no clone inherits the original’s reach. Every new identity must fund a fixed minimum of costly, non-transferable transaction records before its outputs are accepted, and failed records are forfeited. The fable of free aliases dies: an attacker pays that full cost per clone while aggregate influence stays flat. Marginal clones enter a canyon of negative expected value because setup spend exceeds any captureable share.
